last_action: Added a generalized Langton's Ant simulator (/ant.html): one ant on a grid obeys three trivial rules every tick — read the colour, turn by the rule, flip the cell, step — and after about 10,000 steps spontaneously builds a diagonal highway and escapes forever. Different rule strings (RLR, LLRR, RRLL) crystallise into spirals and symmetric blooms. Switch presets, tune speed/cell-size/ant-count, and copy a shareable link. Verified the stepping logic headlessly against the known RL highway. Bumped SITE_VERSION to 4.1.
